newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but off the day's highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but off the day's highs.

text.p: Speculative short covering bolstered CSCE cocoa futures on Tuesday, but steady scale-up selling by the trade kept prices from breaching key resistance levels, market sources said.
Most-active May rose $8 per tonne on the day, to $1,270, having traded from $1,280 to $1,258. Spot March eased $1, to $1,230, while the outer months finished $4 to $5 weaker.

Prices slumped this morning but manufacturer interest at the lows cut into losses. Traders said speculative interest picked up after a series of commission house buy-stops were activated in the May contract between $1,282 and $1,285.
But the rally quickly ran out of steam when May failed to get by critical resistance at $1,291, they added.

On the charts, traders said May would probably continue having problems at $1,291-$1,293. After that a strong psychological level was seen at $1,300. Near-term support was seen toward today's low of $1,360, with the next level put at its life-of-contract low $1,252.
Traders said the latest arrival figures from the Ivory Coast had little impact on today's activity.
Ivorian industry sources said cocoa arrivals at the country's ports were around 880,000 tonnes by February 23, compared with 920,000 tonnes February 24 last season.
One port source noted, however, arrivals were coming in at some 50,000 tonnes a week, about half the rate seen earlier in the month.
Ivorian crop analysts said arrivals to date suggested a total 1996/97 crop of well over one million tonnes, depending on the eventual shape of this year's mid-crop.
While traders said the recent slow down in arrivals was constructive, estimates that the 1996/97 crop could come in over one million tonnes weighed on sentiment.
"If we are looking at a more than one million tonne crop, it is going to offset the bullishness of smaller arrivals," one trader said.
Turnover reached an estimated 7,754 lots today, up slightly from Monday's official tally of 7,494 lots. (( --Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
